preset_question.annual_summary.label: Annual Summary
preset_question.annual_summary.prompt:
Please generate an [Annual Ledger Summary] for me.

This is a comprehensive annual analysis task. Please follow these requirements:

1. Time range: Cover a complete calendar year (start and end dates should be based on the year corresponding to the current data, or as specified by the system/context, if not specified, and the current year is not over, the previous year is used).
2. This is a [Macro Statistics + Multi-dimensional Analysis] task. You can and should call the analyze_bills tool multiple times to complete statistics from different dimensions.
3. Please include at least the following analysis dimensions (you can extend as needed):
   - Annual total income, total expenses, and balance
   - Expense composition by [Category] (Top categories)
   - Expense trends by [Month] (identify volatile or anomalous months)
   - Average daily expenses & Maximum single-day expenses
   - Most frequent expense categories or tags (spending habits)
   - Whether there are obvious phase changes (e.g., beginning of year vs. end of year)
4. During the analysis process:
   - All conclusions must be based on real data obtained through tools
   - No subjective speculation is allowed
5. When outputting the final result, please:
   - Summarize in a natural, "annual review" narrative style
   - Provide 2-4 "data-based personal insights"
   - Provide 1-3 "improvement or recommendation directions for the next year"

Please begin your analysis.

accounting-account-list-help: Select an account to edit. Spending categories are expense accounts.
accounting-used-account-help: An account with transactions keeps its original type and currency.
accounting-asset-rule-generated-help: This interval was generated by its purchase transaction. Edit the parent purchase to change its period, residual value or expense account.
accounting-opening-asset-help: Enter money or asset value you already have when starting this ledger. For example, enter 3,000 if your bank account already holds 3,000. Leave it at 0 if there is no balance. The opening date is when this balance is recorded.
accounting-opening-asset-equity-help: A nonzero balance is saved as an opening transaction with paired changes to this asset and the selected equity account. It represents net assets you already owned and does not count as income or expenses. Record later income, transfers or purchases as separate transactions to avoid counting them twice.
accounting-opening-pair-error: Opening cost and store balance must both be positive or both be zero.
accounting-create-prepaid-first: Create a prepaid asset account first
accounting-create-currency-account: Create an account in the same currency first
accounting-topup-help: Top-up bonuses increase store value; the asset increases by the amount actually paid.
accounting-currency-cost-help: Foreign and custom stored-credit currencies share average costing. Fund through Double entry → Exchange / Top up and spend in the original currency under Expense. A matching expense account is created or reused. Base-currency amounts are estimates for preview. Create custom currencies under Rates & currencies.
accounting-currency-estimate-help: Base-currency amounts are estimated at the average cost when spent, for preview only. Account changes and balancing use actual amounts in the original currency.
accounting-prepaid-currency-help: A separate currency is created for this account. After saving, record the actual payment and credited balance through a top-up. Spending is expensed at the average cost at that time.
accounting-prepaid-average-help: Remaining cost {cost}, credit balance {balance}. Cost per credit: {rate} {currency}. Top-ups combine with remaining cost; spending reduces both proportionally.
accounting-spend-help: Spending uses the ratio of remaining cost to store value at that time, based on a moving weighted average.
accounting-replay-help: Editing past transactions recalculates later spending costs. Insufficient store value prevents saving.
accounting-create-account-first: Create the required accounts in Accounts first.
accounting-action-failed: The action failed. Please try again.
accounting-feature-pending: This feature has not yet been connected to the double-entry ledger.
accounting-delete-account-warning: Delete “{name}”? Accounts with entries or child accounts cannot be deleted. Archive them instead.
accounting-guide-pairing: Each transaction records where value comes from and where it goes. Choose the related accounts and the app creates the paired entries.
accounting-description-asset: Money or items you own and can use, such as cash, bank balances, prepaid cards, and computers.
accounting-example-asset: Receiving wages increases cash. Buying a computer decreases cash and increases fixed assets.
accounting-description-liability: Money you owe, such as credit card balances, loans, and unpaid bills.
accounting-example-liability: Paying with a credit card increases expenses and liabilities. Repaying principal decreases assets and liabilities without recording another expense.
accounting-description-income: Money you earn, grouped by source, such as wages, bonuses, and interest.
accounting-example-income: Receiving wages increases both assets and income. Previous income categories correspond to income accounts here.
accounting-description-expense: Value you spend or consume, grouped by purpose, such as food, transport, and depreciation.
accounting-example-expense: Paying for a meal decreases cash and increases food expenses. Depreciation decreases fixed assets and increases depreciation expense. Previous spending categories correspond to expense accounts.
accounting-description-equity: Net assets you already had when starting the ledger, or capital you contribute, such as opening equity.
accounting-example-equity: Cash you already own can be paired with an equity account without treating it as newly earned income. Balances are still calculated from entries.
accounting-prepaid-entry-help: Prepaid top-ups and spending are available in asset accounts.
accounting-repayment-help: Principal repayments are not expenses. Record interest or fees as separate expenses.
accounting-settings-create-account: Create the required accounts in Settings → Accounts.
accounting-asset-purchase-help: The purchase adds an asset rather than an expense. Set a period and residual value below to create a depreciation / amortization child transaction. Multiple items can share one asset account.
accounting-borrowing-help: Borrowing increases assets and debt, without recording income. Use Debt repayment to repay principal.
accounting-journal-help: Choose from all five account types and enter each debit or credit amount. Total debits must equal total credits. The top amount and calculator edit the selected entry.
accounting-journal-fill-amounts: Enter a positive amount for each row to check the balance.
accounting-journal-complex-edit: Edit transactions with multiple entries in Double entry to preserve every entry.
accounting-journal-dedicated-editor: Use the dedicated prepaid editor for transactions with prepaid face amounts.
accounting-journal-depreciation-help: Record a one-off depreciation expense: decrease the asset and increase the expense on this date. To spread depreciation over a period, create an interval child transaction in Buy asset.
accounting-images-failed: Could not add images. Choose PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files.
accounting-location-failed: Could not locate you. Check location permission and device location services.
accounting-map-config-required: Configure maps in Settings before adjusting the location.
accounting-account-icon-help: Click the icon to change it. Each account and subaccount has its own icon.
stat-saved-filter-help: Save the analysis view, filters and date mode. Weeks, months and years follow the current date; custom dates stay fixed. Select a name above to switch views, and use Save to keep changes.
stat-no-saved-filters: No saved filters yet. Choose Add filter to save the current view.
stat-filter-book-changed: The book has changed. Please reopen the filter.
accounting-children-edit-help: Children are saved in this purchase. Change the period or residual value above to update depreciation; uncheck automatic depreciation to remove it when saving.
accounting-delete-parent-help: Handle linked child transactions before deleting their parent.
accounting-delete-transaction-warning: Delete this transaction? Account balances will be recalculated from the remaining transactions.
accounting-transfer-amount: Increase in the destination asset account
stat-saved-amount-help: Uses stored amounts without recalculating current exchange rates.
stat-native-amount-help: Includes only entries in the selected currency, using their original currency amounts.
stat-unified-help: Filter transactions, then select entries by account type. Charts show period increases, decreases and net changes. Depreciation is allocated over its period without saving daily records.
stat-filtered-assets-help: Note, tag, user, type, related account and amount filters select period changes. Charts, totals and details share these results. Amounts use the selected metric in the base currency. Actual balances retain all history; clear transaction filters to view balance trends.
stat-filtered-depreciation-help: Missing depreciation notes, tags and users inherit the purchase's metadata; type can match either. Amounts use daily depreciation in the base currency. Period expense, accumulated depreciation and remaining value cover the same matched items; the latter two retain each item's complete depreciation history.
stat-income-expense-analysis-help: Analyze income and expense accounts over the selected period using trends, calendars and breakdown charts. Transfer, borrowing, repayment and asset purchase principal are excluded.
stat-assets-liabilities-analysis-help: Owner's equity (net assets) = assets − liabilities. Balances use the end date; changes use the selected period. Bars retain positive and negative directions. Equity accounts record opening capital, contributions and currency clearing; they are not a separate analysis category and are not added again to net assets.
stat-no-data: No data for this period and these filters.
stat-invalid-range: The start date must not be after the end date.
stat-negative-list-help: Negative amounts are shown in a list to preserve the direction of each change.
stat-entry-details-help: Amounts include only matching entries. Depreciation and period transactions show allocated amounts by day. Matching entries from the same transaction and day are combined without saving daily transactions.
stat-base-currency-help: All amounts shown in the base currency, {currency}
stat-balance-help: Balances use the complete history through the selected date, including balances before the period. Parent accounts include their own and descendant postings without double counting.
stat-filter-help: Reporting accounts filter income/expense entries; related accounts filter transactions. Transfer, top-up and exchange principal are excluded from income and expenses. Fees are expenses. Archived accounts remain in historical reports.
stat-estimate-help: Daily allocation replaces month-end depreciation in this display. Totals, trends and account breakdowns share the same estimated basis through today.
stat-depreciation-view-help: Automatic depreciation is allocated across calendar days, starting on the purchase date. Period expense, accumulated depreciation and remaining value use the same basis. Future dates are excluded from incurred costs.
accounting-funding-topup-help: The destination is a recharge card, so this is recorded as a top-up automatically. A separate stored-credit currency records a conversion even at 1:1; equal same-currency funding behaves as a transfer with no income or expense. Use a separate stored-credit currency for unequal amounts. Each account has its own balance and average cost; the note is yours to write.
accounting-exchange-group-help: Each currency is recorded in a child account. The parent groups them without adding balances in different currencies.
accounting-transfer-help: Enter the transfer amount at the top. Destination assets must use the same currency as the source. For another currency, choose Exchange / Top up.
accounting-transfer-no-destination: No other {currency} asset account is available. Create one in the same currency, or choose Exchange / Top up.
accounting-exchange-help: Enter the actual withdrawal including fees at the top, then the actual receipt below. Optional fees use the paying currency. With no fee entered, the actual amounts determine the effective rate.
accounting-rate-missing: Some accounts cannot be converted until an exchange is recorded.
accounting-base-display-help: Shown in the base currency using the recorded cost estimate or a rate derived from this book. Account and entry amounts remain in their original currencies.
accounting-rate-refresh-failed: Could not refresh rates. Existing rates are still available.
accounting-currency-used: This currency is used by an account and cannot be deleted.
accounting-valuation-help: Value all accounts in the main currency using rates derived from exchanges, without changing historical transactions.
accounting-valuation-missing: Complete valuation needs exchange records for: {currencies}
multi-currency-help: Creating an asset account in another currency enables multiple currencies automatically.
multi-currency-required: Create an asset account in another currency to use currency exchange.
accounting-equity-change-help: This transaction's change in equity (assets minus liabilities). Positive increases it; negative decreases it.
accounting-derived-rates-help: Foreign and custom stored-credit currencies both use remaining cost divided by remaining balance. Explicit fees are expensed separately. Missing cost basis is shown without fetching market rates.
accounting-recharge-card-help: A separate currency is created exclusively for this card. Record top-ups to establish its balance and cost; no opening balance is set.
accounting-depreciation-help: Choose an existing asset account. Each purchase has its own interval child transaction, so several items can share the account. Depreciation = purchase price minus expected residual value; charts spread it over the period. Name the item in the note.
accounting-depreciation-default-expense-: Use the default depreciation expense account in the asset's currency. If none exists, it is created when saving the transaction.
accounting-time-zone-invalid-time: This date or time does not exist in the selected time zone. Please choose another time.
accounting-time-zone-help: Times are stored in UTC. This time zone controls date input, display, and daily reports. Changing it preserves each transaction's original UTC instant.
accounting-depreciation-pending: Waiting for the acquisition transaction; depreciation has not started.
accounting-depreciation-locked: The account has been funded. Its original depreciation estimates are locked to preserve historical expenses.
accounting-depreciation-daily-help: Recognize one calendar day's share at a time, with the first day effective at the purchase time. Charts and balances use the same amounts; future dates are excluded from incurred costs.
accounting-account-missing: Account not found; reopen the form.
accounting-search-input: Search notes, accounts or transaction types
stat-activity-help: Opening balance + increases − decreases = closing balance. Internal transfers cancel within the selected group; select an account to see transfers in and out. Balances include booked depreciation and use base currency account costs.
stat-activity-details-help: Amounts show changes in the selected accounts’ balances in the base currency, combined per transaction. Internal transfers have zero net change and are excluded from income and expenses. Derived depreciation links to its acquisition transaction.
stat-balance-date-help: Balances are calculated as of the period end; changes cover the selected start and end dates. Asset use includes related accumulated depreciation and preserves the full transaction history.
stat-depreciation-date-help: Period depreciation uses daily estimates within the selected dates. Accumulated depreciation, carrying value and status are determined at the period end. Charts and details use the same assets.
stat-asset-usage-help: Select Total assets to filter ordinary accounts, prepaid cards or fixed assets.
accounting-template-guide-payments: Cash, WeChat, Bank card and Alipay are payment accounts. For an expense, choose a payment account and then an expense account such as Food. WeChat starts with a sample balance of 1,000 yuan, offset by WeChat opening equity. Open its opening transaction on the home page to enter your actual balance.
accounting-template-guide-card: The Metro transit card has its own stored currency and starts at zero. In Double entry, use Currency exchange / top-up and select the card as the receiving account. Enter the amount paid and the amount credited to the card. Select the card and a transport expense account when spending; the app estimates the yuan value from the remaining cost.
accounting-template-guide-fixed: Computers, phones and other items can share Valuables without separate subaccounts. Use Asset purchase in Double entry to record each price, depreciation period and expected residual value. Each purchase contains its own depreciation child. Purchasing moves assets; later depreciation becomes an expense. Statistics show daily amortization.
accounting-template-guide-liability: Credit card and Huabei track outstanding debt and start at zero. Record credit purchases by increasing an expense and a liability in Double entry. For repayment, choose a payment account and the liability; repayment does not create another expense.
accounting-template-guide-income: Salary and Other are common income sources. Select an income account and the receiving asset account. Record borrowing and card top-ups in Double entry.
accounting-template-guide-expense: Food includes Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Snacks and Drinks. Transport includes Subway, Bus and Taxi. Each expense is posted once. Depreciation expense comes from the interval children of purchases.
accounting-template-guide-equity: WeChat opening equity offsets the sample WeChat balance of 1,000 yuan. It represents money owned before bookkeeping and belongs to net assets rather than salary income. To adjust the balance, edit both entries of the opening transaction and keep them balanced.
accounting-template-book-help: New books use a starter template with payment accounts, Credit card / Huabei, food and transport expenses, a transit card with its own currency, and Valuables. Each purchase has its own depreciation period and residual value, so individual items do not need separate accounts. WeChat has a sample opening balance of 1,000 yuan; adjust it to your actual balance. Other accounts start at zero. Data is stored on this device and can be exported as a JSON backup.
accounting-period-purchase-help: Choose an existing asset account. Each purchase has its own interval child transaction, so several items can share the account. Depreciation = purchase price minus expected residual value; charts spread it over the period. Name the item in the note.
accounting-period-posting: Save interval transactions and spread consumption over time
accounting-period-posting-help: Each period is stored as one interval transaction. Reports allocate overlapping time; the future portion does not yet count as expense or reduce the asset.
accounting-period-range-help: Includes the start and excludes the end; the amount covers the whole period.
accounting-purchase-depreciation-account: This account can hold several items. Configure depreciation when adding each purchase, and edit it from that purchase transaction.
accounting-template-guide-asset: Cash, WeChat, Bank card and Alipay record money. Valuables holds computers, phones and other items, with a separate depreciation period for each purchase.
accounting-paired-amount-help: Enter the amount once at the top. Two equal entries are created automatically, using the first account’s currency.
accounting-paired-no-destination: No eligible {currency} account is available. Create one, or use Custom entries for a complex transaction.
accounting-sync-no-remote: No remote books on this service yet. You can upload the current book first.
accounting-sync-help: Sync books incrementally with WebDAV. Concurrent versions are retained; resolve conflicts to resume the ledger and statistics.
accounting-sync-provider-mismatch: This book is linked to {provider}. Switch to that sync provider in Settings.
accounting-import-summary: {accounts} accounts and {transactions} transactions. A new book will be created.
accounting-import-current-only: Supports JSON books in the current 2.0 format.
accounting-payment-disabled: Cannot be used as a payment source
github-sync-help: Create a repository with a README and use an existing branch. The token needs Contents read and write access to this repository. Configuration is saved in this browser.
accounting-choose-book-help: Sync is connected. Choose an existing book or name a new one.
accounting-empty-remote-books: No remote books yet. Create one below.
accounting-import-double-entry-help: Expenses increase costs and reduce the selected asset or increase its liability. Income and refunds reverse the corresponding entries. Map each payment method to an account. Composite payments use the statement amount without guessing funding or discount splits. Existing bill IDs are skipped. Full accounting backups restore as separate books.
accounting-import-no-account: No eligible payment accounts. Create an asset or liability account first.
accounting-import-book-changed: The book has changed. Open a new import preview.
